Separate cooling towers are considered for direct cooling and indirect cooling circuit. 2.0 Permitting Study Requirement The envisaged project of setting up a carbon capture facility in the existing Burns Harbor Plant of Cliffs includes systems handling toxic/hazardous waste materials (solid, liquid, or gaseous). It includes handling wastewater as well as spent chemicals. To dispose of such waste, permits are required from appropriate agencies before commissioning the project facilities. The envisaged system will also contain high-raised towers. Several permits need to be acquired from various authorities for the construction of the proposed facilities for the envisaged project, as is the statutory requirement by these authorities. These permits can be required at various stages of the project implementation spanning the period of pre- construction, during construction, and before the commencement of start-up & operation of the plant. The permit validates the plans of the owner of the proposed plant and ensures that all the guidelines for construction, operations, and waste stream treatment/disposal are followed. The required permits can be categorized into different sub-sections of Federal and State permits, biological and cultural, water, waste, regional and local permits. The Federal and State permits include the air permit, the permit for nucleonic devices, and the permit related to the FAA Notice of the proposed construction form 7460-1. An air permit is required by industries that have the potential to release waste gases or particles into the air. The type of air permit required for each emission source may vary depending on several factors such as emission source category, their potential to emit, types of equipment and operations, and the area where the emission source is located. The biological and cultural permits include the water quality review.
